metadata.description: Bring up the auth stack (keycloak-service + keycloak-store-postgres + keycloak-mailpit). The compose.dev.yaml overlay (feature 039) seeds the grumpyrobot realm on a fresh volume via --import-realm. Run `node scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs` first (mints auth.env incl. the realm client secrets). Add --args=--profile=vault to include vault-service (prod posture).

Bring up the mcm stack test infra + mc-service (--profile app). Run `node scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs` first (mints mcm.env) and `pnpm nx build mc-service` (mc-service:latest is local-only; without it this fails with `pull access denied`, which is not a registry login problem). Bring up auth first (manual ordering). Add bff-nonsecure / bff-secure / agents via docker compose --profile.

Bring up the AI agent layer under the mcm compose stack (HEAVY variant: gateway + 3 MCP + movie-assistant-store-postgres checkpointer). Fetches the agent-gateway Keycloak client secret and injects it so tool calls work. Prereqs: up-auth + up-mcm + host Ollama. Distinct from up-agents-prod (the light docker-run/MemorySaver E2E variant).
Bring up the audit stack (agent-audit-opensearch append-only sink). Run `node scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs` first (mints audit.env).
Bring up the observability stack (LangFuse + otel-lgtm + opa-service + unleash-service). Run `node scripts/gen-dev-secrets.mjs` first (mints observability.env).
Convenience: bring up auth (Keycloak) then the mcm app stack in order (auth before mc-service, FR-006). Run `pnpm nx build mc-service` first (see up-mcm).

options.command: docker compose -p mcm -f infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/mcm.compose.yaml --env-file infrastructure-as-code/docker/stacks/mcm.env --profile app --profile bff-nonsecure --profile bff-secure --profile agents --profile agents-metro down

metadata.description: Tear down all four stacks (keeps external volumes).

Deploy the containerized production-node agent stack (gateway + movie-mcp + web-api-mcp; host Ollama, MemorySaver) for local agent E2E. Rebuilds the 4 agent/MCP images from the checkout by default (feature 041 — skipping made CI test stale images); pass --args=--no-build for a fast local loop (refused under CI).
Remove the containerized production-node agent stack (gateway + movie-mcp + web-api-mcp).

Static resource-naming gate (features 019 + 020): assert every Docker volume/network name, and every container_name == service key == convention. Pass --args=--section=volumes|networks|containers|ollama|all (default all).

Static inline-secret gate (feature 021): assert no tracked compose file holds a clear-text credential — every secret-shaped key / password URL / auth literal must be a ${VAR} reference. Pass --args=--selftest to validate the detector.

Run the OWASP ZAP DAST baseline (non-destructive: spider + passive) against the local stack, authenticated as the E2E test user. Reports → security/zap/reports/. Prereqs: auth + mcm stacks up (add --profile agents for the gateway target). Pass --args='--mode full' + DAST_ALLOW_ACTIVE=1 for the destructive active scan (disposable stacks only, FR-017). See docs/runbooks/dast-scanning.md.

Run the keyless SAST + SCA static scan (Semgrep code SAST over TS/JS + Python; cargo/pnpm/pip audit over the three dependency graphs) and write a consolidated, risk-normalized report to security/sast/reports/. No running app stack required. Prereqs: uv/uvx, a Rust toolchain with cargo-audit, pnpm. Pass --args='--scope changed --base <ref>' to scope Semgrep to changed files (SCA still runs full). Gate the report with `node scripts/check-sast-findings.mjs`. See docs/runbooks/sast-scanning.md.

Generate or refresh the OKF knowledge bundle at openwiki/ (feature 043) by running scripts/wiki-generate.mjs, which resolves the generator's provider and model from MCM_WIKI_PROVIDER (anthropic | fireworks; feature 078) — this target deliberately names NO provider or model, because nx lets a target's env overwrite the calling job's and the workflow could then never switch it (078 research R4). The launcher maps the provider's credential at the point of use, loads the usage tap, and passes WIKI_RUN_MESSAGE as one argv element with no shell. THE PER-TURN OUTPUT CAP IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS NOT A TASTE CHOICE. History: openwiki <=0.4.x never set `maxTokens`, so @langchain/anthropic resolved the cap by prefix-matching the model id against a hard-coded table and falling back to 4096 on a miss. The id pinned at the time was absent from that table, so it silently got 4096 — and a turn truncated at that cap before it opens a tool_use block yields an assistant message with ZERO tool calls, which is exactly LangGraph's ReAct stop condition. The graph then exits cleanly, openwiki exits 0, Nx reports success, and nothing is written. That was the measured ~50% zero-page rate (research 2026-08-01, specs/044-openwiki-automation-migration/HANDOFF-generator-reliability-ANSWER.md), caught live at turn 25 of a real run: stop_reason=max_tokens, output_tokens=4096, no tool call. AS OF openwiki 0.5.2 the defect is fixed upstream — `resolveAnthropicMaxOutputTokens` supplies an explicit 16384 for any claude-(haiku|sonnet|opus)-(4|5) id — but that fix is INVISIBLE AT RUNTIME and a model rename or a vendor change would silently undo it, so OPENWIKI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is set here EXPLICITLY rather than inherited from a vendor table. openwiki reads it ahead of everything else, which makes this value, not the table, the one that reaches the model. Before changing a model id in scripts/wiki-provider.mjs or OPENWIKI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS here, run `node --test scripts/__tests__/wiki-maintain.guard.test.mjs` — it fails an unset or too-small cap, a model id openwiki's own resolver does not match, and any id that would land on the 4096 fallback. A run message may be supplied in the WIKI_RUN_MESSAGE env var, which scopes the run to named pages (feature 044). It must never travel through `nx --args`, which strips its quoting so the message reaches the generator as a dozen separate words and the run goes UNSCOPED (measured 2026-07-30); the launcher passes it as one argv element with no shell at all (feature 078). With the variable unset the refresh is unscoped, as before. ALWAYS invoke through this target, never the bare CLI: it sets OPENWIKI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1, and the tool reports usage telemetry to a third-party analytics host by DEFAULT (FR-030). The dev container's egress allowlist would block that, but the Windows host has no such protection — so the opt-out lives here, in the invocation path, rather than in setup docs a developer could skip. Uses --update (not --init): it creates the bundle when absent, so the interactive onboarding and the ~/.openwiki/.env it would write are avoided entirely. Scope and redaction rules are hand-authored in openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md, which the tool reads but never rewrites. Gate the result with `pnpm nx okf-lint infrastructure-as-code`. See docs/runbooks/devcontainer.md.

MANUAL rebuild of operator-named derived pages (features 044/078/098) — PAID: pass --args="--pages runbooks/x.md,projects/y.md" (add --dry-run to print the run messages and invoke nothing). Routine freshness is NOT this target: since feature 098 the coding session that changes a page's source refreshes the page with node scripts/wiki-refresh.mjs in the same PR, and the required okf check (V17) blocks a stale one. A canonical, unknown or missing-source page is refused with exit 2 before anything is spent. Each slice invokes the generator through `wiki-update`, with the provider chosen by MCM_WIKI_PROVIDER (CI: fireworks, keyed by FIREWORKS_API_KEY or MCM_FIREWORKS_API_KEY; the anthropic default takes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or MCM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). ALWAYS invoke through this target (or the wiki-maintain workflow) rather than calling the generator yourself: it verifies every page by what actually landed in the working tree, by bundle conformance and governance, and records each landed page's source fingerprint — never trusting the generator's exit status (feature 043 measured 12 minutes of paid work, one index.md written, exit 0, reported as success). In CI, WIKI_JOB_DEADLINE stops a running generator before the job's window ends. Exit 0 = every named page landed; 1 = one did not (they are listed); 2 = refused before any spend. See docs/runbooks/wiki-maintenance.md.

Run the OKF conformance gate over the openwiki/ bundle (feature 043): front matter parses, required `type` present, ISO-8601 timestamps, repo-relative `resource` links resolve, an index.md per directory, no orphaned concepts. Offline and keyless — external links are shape-checked, never fetched. Fail-closed: an absent or partially-written bundle fails rather than passing vacuously, and there is no skip flag. Drift (a source newer than the concept citing it) is reported as a WARNING and never affects the exit code. Pass --args=--selftest to validate the detector first.

Run the OpenWiki governance gate over this repository (feature 044): every documentation path carries a declared regeneration policy, `actor: generator` appears only inside openwiki/, every event-driven entry names its events, every relocated load-bearing passage still matches its fingerprint (a REMOVED one fails as a removal, not as nothing-to-compare), no protected passage sits on a concept that cites a source, CLAUDE.md holds only its index and its three machine-managed regions, every index entry and assistant-surface link resolves, and every concept is provably exactly one of derived or authoritative. Offline, keyless, fail-closed — a missing or unparseable governance file is a violation, and there is deliberately NO skip flag and no allowlist: a rejected page is fixed in openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md and regenerated. Pass --args=--selftest to validate the detector first, --args='--explain <path>' to see which policy entry governs a path, or --args='--fingerprint <concept> "<anchor>"' to compute the value protected.yaml should carry. See docs/runbooks/wiki-maintenance.md.

Run the keyless infra-image CVE scan (feature 035): enumerate the third-party images pulled in infrastructure-as-code/** (excluding the six jumbleknot/* images cd-deploy already scans, and ${..}-interpolated refs), scan each with Trivy, and write a normalized report to security/infra-images/reports/. Prereq: Trivy on PATH + Docker (Linux/CI — not the Windows dev box). Pass --args='--list' to enumerate only (no Trivy). Gate the report with `node scripts/check-infra-image-findings.mjs`. See docs/runbooks/infra-image-scanning.md.

Feature 038 — build the heavy dev-container toolchain image locally from .devcontainer/toolchain.Dockerfile and tag it mcm-devcontainer:local (the offline / no-forge one-time fallback that makes the devcontainer.json BASE_IMAGE default resolve; SC-011). The fast path is instead pulling the CI-published forge image via MCM_DEVCONTAINER_IMAGE. Prereq: Docker. Pass --args='--tag <ref>' to override the tag. See docs/runbooks/devcontainer.md.

Run every CHEAP check CI runs, before pushing: all guardrail gates (selftest + scan), the scripts/__tests__ unit tests, then lint + typecheck + unit for mcm-app. Deliberately excludes app-e2e, dast, the integration tiers and the SAST/SCA scan — those need the CI runner, a live stack or an emulator. Exists because CI has ONE runner and app-e2e is ~35 min, so a red push for an offline-knowable reason is disproportionately expensive. Pass --args='--gates-only' to skip lint/typecheck/unit. See openwiki/invariants/testing-tiers.md and openwiki/invariants/feature-validation-checklist.md.
